heading: INT. PAWNSHOP - FORMER BANK VAULT - NIGHT

units.text: INT. PAWNSHOP - FORMER BANK VAULT - NIGHT
A round steel door hangs open on massive hinges.
Inside: glass cases of watches, guitars on hooks, a rack of cameras, a wall of safety-deposit boxes now repurposed as shelves.
A single caged bulb swings, throwing shadows that slide like water.
MOSES ACHTERBERG (60s, pawnbroker, green visor, suspenders) sits behind a scarred counter, counting a stack of bills.
A baseball bat leans within reach.
In front of the counter, TORVALD NKEMELU (30s, shaved head, leather jacket, a canvas bag at his feet) taps a ring on the glass.
Next to him, SIMONE ARQUETTE (30s, red scarf, tight smile, a laptop bag across her chest) studies the shelves.
That ring is worth four hundred.
units.name: MOSES

units.text: It's worth eight.
units.name: TORVALD

units.text: Not to me.
units.name: MOSES

units.text: It's his grandmother's.
units.name: TORVALD

units.text: Then he should have kept it.
units.name: MOSES

units.text: Simone drifts toward the deposit boxes, running a finger along the brass doors.
She pauses at number 214.
Her smile tightens.
Moses, what's in these?
units.name: SIMONE

units.text: Inventory.
units.name: MOSES

units.text: All of it?
units.name: SIMONE

units.text: All of it.
units.name: MOSES

units.text: Torvald slides the canvas bag closer with his heel.
Moses watches the bag, not the man.
What's in that?
units.name: MOSES

units.text: Watches. Maybe six.
units.name: TORVALD

units.text: Let's see them.
units.name: MOSES

units.text: Torvald lifts the bag onto the counter.
Unzips it a few inches.
Moses leans in.
Simone steps up behind Torvald, hand on his shoulder.
The door at the back of the vault creaks.
Everyone turns.
A new figure steps out of the dark: DETECTIVE MARISOL VEGA-LINDSTROM (40s, gray blazer, badge clipped at the hip, tired eyes).
She holds a coffee in one hand and nothing in the other.
Evening.
units.name: MARISOL

units.text: Nobody speaks.
Moses's fingers drift toward the bat.
Moses. Don't.
units.name: MARISOL

units.text: I haven't done anything.
units.name: MOSES

units.text: That's what worries me.
units.name: MARISOL

units.text: She crosses to the counter, sets her coffee down.
Looks at Torvald, then Simone, then the bag.
Torvald. Simone. Nice to see you out of the car.
units.name: MARISOL

units.text: Torvald and Simone exchange a look.
Torvald's hand edges toward the zipper.
Simone's hand edges toward her laptop bag.
Both of you. Hands where I can see them.
units.name: MARISOL

units.text: Neither obeys.
Moses lifts the bat an inch off the wall.
Marisol pulls her jacket aside to show the holster.
Everybody in this room needs to relax.
units.name: MARISOL

units.text: Simone laughs once, a sharp, high sound.
We're just selling watches.
units.name: SIMONE

units.text: Are you? Because the last six watches in this county were stolen from Dr. Hartwell's house on Tuesday.
units.name: MARISOL

units.text: Not these.
units.name: TORVALD

units.text: Prove it.
units.name: MARISOL

units.text: Torvald and Simone move at once.
Torvald hurls the bag at Marisol's chest.
Simone grabs the laptop bag and swings.
Marisol ducks, draws, and shoves Simone back against the wall.
Moses brings the bat down on the counter with a crack that echoes through the vault.
Glass shatters.
Watches scatter across the floor like beads.
Down! Everyone down!
units.name: MARISOL

units.text: Torvald tackles Moses over the counter.
They crash into a rack of guitars.
Strings scream.
Simone drops the laptop bag and dives for the vault door.
Marisol fires once into the ceiling.
The bulb explodes.
Darkness falls.
In the black, four people breathe, wounded, cursing, panting.
Glass crunches.
Something metallic rolls and stops.
A flashlight clicks on in Marisol's hand.
Its beam finds Simone at the door, one foot out.
Torvald and Moses lie tangled on the floor, wrestling for the bat.
Nobody leaves.
units.name: MARISOL

units.text: Simone raises her hands.
The beam rests on her red scarf.
Torvald lets go of the bat.
Moses lets go of Torvald.
Marisol steps over the broken glass, crouches, picks up a single gold watch.
She turns it over.
Reads the back.
"To Walter, with love."
units.name: MARISOL

units.text: She looks at Moses.
Hartwell's father.
units.name: MARISOL

units.text: Moses lowers his eyes.
Simone sags against the steel door.
Torvald, lying on his back, laughs quietly at the ceiling.
